transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Aperion EM), Ravi Singh (Aperion ML Eng), Janelle Ortiz (Aperion Product), Marco Leone (Aperion Infra)

Summary:
Aperion is evaluating options to power real-time personalization on the product detail and homepage journeys. Primary concerns: p99 latency < 75ms for embed+rerank path, cost per 1M requests, ability to run private (VPC) due to PCI-like data controls, and a hybrid architecture that uses local vector DB for first-pass then Redwood rerank. They are leaning toward a Dedicated POC to validate throughput and tail latency but want to compare hosted economics and Private (VPC) network options.

Topics:
- Current stack & constraints
- Embedding dimensionality and tradeoffs
- Vector DB fanout vs single-shard rerank
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) pros and cons
- Latency benchmarking and tooling
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs

Action items (recorded):
- See action_items field

Transcript: (periodic timestamps, transcription imperfect)
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros and then we'll jump in — i'm Maya from Redwood, and Samir's our solutions engineer.
[00:15] Olivia: Hi all, Olivia here. we own search and personalization. trying to get this lined up for the holiday ramp.
[00:20] Ravi: ravi here, im the engineer who will run the POC and the benchmarks.
[00:25] Janelle: Janelle - product - i'll own acceptance criteria.
[00:29] Marco: Marco - infra - i care about network, kms, and firewalls.

[00:35] Samir: Great. can you give us a quick picture of your current runtime for embeddings + rerank? like where do you compute embeddings, what vector DB, QPS?
[00:48] Olivia: Sure. currently we compute embeddings at ingest using a CPU pipeline on our ETL cluster, store 512-d vectors in Milvus in a multi-AZ cluster. Queries hit a lightweight retriever that returns top 200 and then we run a BERT-based reranker in our services — it's slow tho, p99 is about 400ms for rerank alone.
[01:05] Ravi: Our steady QPS on search is ~120 rps but during promo spikes it hits 800 rps for a few minutes. We're trying to keep p99 end-to-end under 120ms, ideally 75ms on the embed+rerank so product feels snappy.
[01:24] Samir: ok understood. are you open to doing embedding compute at request time vs precomputed? That changes fanout patterns.
[01:30] Olivia: We prefer precomputed for catalog, but for personalized pieces we sometimes compute session-level embeddings on the fly. so hybrid.
[01:38] Samir: that's common. for hybrid routing the typical Redwood pattern is local vdb first-pass (we can integrate w/ Milvus) and then call a Redwood-hosted or dedicated reranker which accepts embeddings or IDs. That reduces the amount of rerank calls.
[01:54] Marco: quick security Q: if you host in Redwood hosted, does traffic traverse public internet? we need VPC peering or private link.
[02:02] Maya: short answer: hosted can be used but for strict network controls we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) which provides customer-controlled networking and optional customer-managed KMS. hosted has TLS and encryption at rest but no private peering in the basic plan.
[02:18] Marco: ok, that's important.

[02:25] Ravi: about dimensionality — we use 512 dims now. any recommendations? we care about throughput and vector storage cost.
[02:32] Samir: 512 is common, but there are clear tradeoffs. lower dims like 128-256 can cut storage and CPU during fanout significantly. Quality delta depends on model; we typically run a small sweep. for rerank, the initial retriever can use compact dims and then the reranker uses the full-context model for final scoring.
[02:54] Olivia: hmm so you're saying do small-embedding index to limit fanout and then call rerank with a full LM? what does that do to p99?
[03:02] Samir: it usually helps. fewer candidates -> fewer expensive rerank calls. but you need to tune recall. also Redwood supports caching of prefix K V cache and rerank results to reduce repeated cost. (transcription: k v cache mentioned as KV cache but sometimes spoken as k v kase)
[03:20] Ravi: i want to understand end-to-end numbers. can you share examples of how Dedicated performs at say 800 rps with a 200 candidate rerank?
[03:31] Samir: rough numbers: with dedicated RTX-class GPUs and batching, we can hit ~900-1200 qps for cheap embed-only requests if quantized; but for a heavy rerank path with large LM scoring 200 candidates you'll push throughput down — batching helps but tail latency matters. For your p99 75ms target, we'd likely do a two-step flow: 1) local index fanout (50-200) 2) call Redwood rerank on top 10 with a smaller scoring model tuned for latency. Also consider model quantization and sharded rerank.
[03:58] Janelle: can you quantify 'smaller scoring model'? like what model family?
[04:03] Samir: often a smaller cross-encoder distilled variant — think a lighter seq2seq ranker or a 3B transformer with optimizations; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization/instance types. note: smaller model sacrifices some accuracy but often acceptable for UX.
[04:20] Olivia: we absolutely need to measure recall drop. we will provide eval pairs.

[04:28] Marco: on private deployments, what does network setup look like? do we need an appliance?
[04:34] Maya: Private gives you a control plane in Redwood, but inference nodes run in your VPC or on-prem. we support VPC peering, private link, or an on-prem package. infra folks install a small agent and we orchestrate. KMS integration for keys is supported.
[04:51] Marco: and audit logs? we need request-level logs for compliance.
[04:56] Samir: yes, Private & Dedicated include richer audit logs and can ship them to your SIEM. hosted also has logs but limited retention unless you buy the add-on.
[05:06] Ravi: what's the typical cost delta between hosted and dedicated for heavy fanout?
[05:10] Maya: hosted is simpler and good for low-to-medium scale. Dedicated reserved capacity amortizes GPU costs and is cheaper at sustained high QPS. Example: for consistent 400-800 rps with heavy rerank, Dedicated can be 30-50% cheaper per-token after commit discounts. exact numbers depend on model choice, quantization, and caching.
[05:31] Olivia: what about burst handling around promo spikes — we have short blasts to 2k rps sometimes.
[05:37] Samir: Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscale heuristics; we can configure overflow to a hosted fallback to avoid cold starts. Also pre-warming and continuous batching helps. private on-prem can be limited by your infra.
[05:53] Janelle: any pitfalls with vector DB integration? we've got Milvus and some older vector service.
[05:59] Samir: common issues: sharding mismatch, replica lag, stale vectors during reindex, and fanout amplification due to high-dim neighbors. Redwood provides connectors and recommends small-batch reads and consistent sharding key strategies. we often suggest a narrow fanout (50-100) and then rerank.
[06:18] Ravi: latency budget break-down — can you propose where time should be spent end-to-end?
[06:22] Samir: rough split for a 75ms target: network + retrieval 20ms, scoring/rerank 35-45ms, application overhead and merges 10-20ms. So rerank needs to be optimized heavily.
[06:36] Olivia: does Redwood do streaming rerank or do we wait for full response?
[06:40] Samir: rerank typically returns final scored list; Redwood also supports streaming generation for text but for rankers we return once scoring is complete. there are experimental approaches to incremental ranking but they add complexity.
[06:53] Marco: for benchmarking — what do we need from our side to run an apples-to-apples test?
[06:58] Samir: sample traffic profile (qps distribution), a small eval dataset with relevancy labels, blackbox latency targets, network topology, and access to a test Milvus instance or snapshot. we'll run a baseline on hosted and then a dedicated config.
[07:15] Olivia: we can assemble that. we'll anonymize product ids.
[07:18] Ravi: question on caching — if we cache rerank results, how do you handle staleness when product metadata changes?
[07:25] Samir: we version cache keys by vector fingerprint and metadata version; TTLs can be tuned. Redwood supports auto-invalidations for key events.
[07:36] Janelle: regulatory: do you support disk encryption via customer-managed keys?
[07:40] Maya: yes on Private and Dedicated you can plug your KMS/HSM. hosted supports provider-managed keys by default; we offer Bring-Your-Own-KMS on enterprise plans.
[07:52] Marco: what about redwood's SLA for dedicated?
[07:55] Maya: Dedicated has a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency SLOs per instance class; we'll share the doc.
[08:02] Olivia: ok next i'm worried about implementation effort — how long to stand up a Dedicated POC?
[08:08] Samir: typically 1-2 weeks for provisioning and connectors + another 1-2 weeks for benchmarking depending on sample data readiness. Private on-prem is longer due to network and infra setup.
[08:20] Ravi: can we test quantized models? we saw quality drop sometimes with aggressive quantizashun.
[08:27] Samir: yes, Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles; we run a quality sweep during POC to pick the least-impactful profile. usually int8 or mixed 8-bit works well for scoring models.
[08:41] Maya: quick re-cap of options: Hosted = fastest to start, limited network controls; Dedicated = reserved capacity, private networking, cheaper at scale; Private = full VPC/on-prem control, more setup but aligns with compliance.
[08:58] Olivia: sounds good. if we aim for p99 75ms we'll start with a Dedicated POC and compare a hosted fallback.
[09:05] Janelle: acceptance criteria: p99 < 120ms in first week, then target 75ms; recall within 2% of current baseline on top-k.
[09:15] Maya: noted. we'll send a proposed scope and timeline.

[09:22] (wrap up)
[09:25] Maya: next steps again: i'll send pricing, Samir sends benchmark config. Ravi you'll send eval data and QPS profile. Marco send network constraints. we'll schedule POC kick-off.
[09:40] Olivia: thanks everyone. this was helpful.
[09:43] Maya: thanks all.
